title: Exploring Containers
description: Containers from first principles: what they are, the runtimes underneath them, Docker and Podman as tools, and the security/supply-chain discipline production demands.

items.title: Getting Docker Running on Your Machine
items.content_html: Install Docker or Podman on Linux, macOS, or Windows from the command line — no Docker Desktop. Verify it works before writing a single Dockerfile.

items.title: Living With a Partial Migration
items.content_html: Running a monolith and a handful of extracted services together is the normal, long-term state of most real migrations — not a failure to eventually fix.

items.title: Containerizing the First Slice
items.content_html: Pull one validated seam out of the monolith and run it as its own container, side by side with the monolith, without betting the whole migration on it yet.

items.title: Finding the Seams: How to Scope a Microservice
items.content_html: Four signals that tell you a piece of a monolith is a real service boundary, not just a convenient folder — and the distributed-monolith trap that comes from ignoring them.

items.title: Why the Monolith Has to Move
items.content_html: Understand why 'get off the VMs' is really two separate problems, and why containerizing the monolith as-is is a legitimate first step, not a shortcut.

items.title: Sharing It With Your Team
items.content_html: A container that only runs on your laptop hasn't solved the problem yet. Tag, push, and pull an image through a container registry.

items.title: Debugging a Container That Won't Behave
items.content_html: Diagnose a container that exits immediately or runs but doesn't respond — docker logs, docker inspect, docker exec, and the 0.0.0.0 gotcha.

items.title: Building and Running Your Image
items.content_html: docker build and docker run, the gap between a successful build and a working container, and how to pass secrets in without baking them into the image.

items.title: Writing Your First Dockerfile
items.content_html: Write a working Dockerfile for the app you already built — line by line, with the defaults that keep it small, cacheable, and not running as root.

items.title: What Is a Container, Really?
items.content_html: The real mental model for containers: a normal process the kernel agrees to isolate, not a smaller virtual machine. Covers the image vs. container distinction.

items.title: Overview
items.content_html: Two paths into containerization for developers: containerizing a single app for the first time, or breaking a monolith out of VMs. Start here.

items.title: Home
items.content_html: A progressive guide to containerization — from what a container actually is, to the runtimes underneath it, to running it securely in production.
